decisions.decision: How should classification predictions be served?
decisions.context: Millions of incoming documents arrive daily, with strong seasonal volume swings; several teams consume the results.

alternatives.label: Hybrid online/offline model serving
pros: Variable volume: route work between online and batch paths
Cost efficiency: batch work can reduce per-item overhead
cons: Operational simplicity: two serving paths to maintain

alternatives.label: Data batch based model serving
pros: Cost efficiency: scheduled batches suit high volume
cons: Timeliness: results wait for batch runs

alternatives.label: Microservice based model serving
pros: Timeliness: results available through a real-time service
cons: Variable volume: capacity must handle peak demand

decisions.rationale: Variable seasonal volume decides the choice: batch processing can absorb bulk work while an online path supports time-sensitive requests. This costs more operational effort than one serving path.
consequences: Operate and monitor online and batch paths.
Define how consumers retrieve results from either path.

decisions.decision: How should incoming documents be processed?
decisions.context: The system must ingest millions of documents per day, and volume changes considerably by season.

alternatives.label: Batch-based data processing
pros: Cost efficiency: group work into batches
Variable volume: schedule capacity around demand
cons: Timeliness: results may wait for a batch window

alternatives.label: Real-time, stream-based data processing
cons: Cost efficiency: maintain continuous processing capacity

decisions.rationale: Cost efficiency and seasonal volume decide the choice: batch processing can group the large workload and adjust run capacity. The trade-off is that some classifications wait for the next batch.
consequences: Set batch size and processing cadence to meet business timeliness needs.
Scale batch capacity for seasonal peaks.

decisions.decision: How should processing scale across the document workload?
decisions.context: Daily volume is in the millions and varies over the year, so processing needs to run in parallel to handle peaks.

alternatives.label: Data partitioning in data pipeline
pros: High throughput: partitions enable parallel processing
Variable volume: distribute work across available capacity
cons: Cost efficiency: partitioning and coordination add overhead

alternatives.label: Data pipeline per data set
pros: Operational isolation: dedicated pipeline per dataset
cons: Variable volume: scaling across pipelines may be uneven

alternatives.label: No parallel data processing
pros: Cost efficiency: no parallel processing overhead

decisions.rationale: High throughput decides the choice: partitioning enables parallel work within the pipeline. The trade-off is added coordination overhead, which must be weighed against throughput and peak capacity needs.
consequences: Choose partition keys and manage skewed workloads.
Provision parallel capacity for seasonal peaks.

decisions.decision: How should classification quality be monitored?
decisions.context: Operators need to see when classification quality drifts, which requires monitoring production behavior and outcomes.

alternatives.label: Model performance monitoring
pros: Quality drift visibility: observe model performance parameters
cons: Operational response: measures need suitable feedback data

alternatives.label: Monitoring or logging data and predictions
pros: Operational response: retain inputs and predictions for investigation
cons: Quality drift visibility: logs alone do not establish model quality

alternatives.label: No in-production monitoring
cons: Quality drift visibility: operators lack production monitoring

decisions.rationale: Quality drift visibility decides the choice because the brief explicitly requires operators to detect it. This choice depends on having suitable feedback to measure performance; the design space does not specify how to obtain that feedback.
consequences: Define performance measures and drift thresholds.
Determine how classification outcomes or labels become available.

uncovered: How to obtain timely ground truth or other feedback for measuring classification quality.
Latency and freshness targets for results consumed by teams.
Document retention, privacy, and access controls for an insurer's data.
LLM selection, prompt or model version management, and fallback behavior.
Team-facing result schema, delivery contract, and failure handling.
Seasonal capacity limits and cost targets.
